page: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The hardware features 192 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS Graviton4 Neoverse-V2 design running at 2.7 GHz, with single-threaded execution per core and no hyperthreading overhead. It provides 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, and no GPU hardware accelerators are present. Network connectivity is delivered with a 50 Gbps baseline interface.

Benchmark results highlight extreme multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth driven by the 192 dedicated physical cores and DDR5 memory controllers. The server reaches top-tier results in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 959.97 GB/sec, and memory read bandwidth exceeding 897 GB/sec for large un-cached blocks. In operational benchmarks, the platform delivers top-tier performance for static web serving (136.65 GB/sec) and in-memory key-value workflows, achieving 360.85 million Redis SET operations per second. PassMark database tests and Clang compilation metrics also rank in the top percentile.

The primary tradeoff lies in single-threaded performance, where single-core Geekbench and compression metrics sit in the middle 50% percentile due to the conservative 2.7 GHz clock rate. Similarly, lacking discrete GPU hardware, raw token generation speeds for large language models remain low compared to accelerated platforms. Cost efficiency is qualitative: the bare-metal architecture eliminates hypervisor tax, giving maximum return on investment for highly parallel, horizontally scaled, and memory-intensive distributed enterprise workloads.

This server type is suitable for large-scale container clusters, high-concurrency microservices, massive in-memory databases, continuous integration build matrices, and distributed stream data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.metal-48xl is a bare-metal general-purpose server configured with 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 cores (Neoverse-V2) running at 2.7 GHz and 768 GB of DDR5 memory. The platform features a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, a 50 Gbps baseline network link, and operates without bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place the server in the top tier for multi-core compute throughput, DDR5 memory bandwidth, Clang compilation, and in-memory database throughput, logging 360.85 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-core execution speeds and unaccelerated LLM text generation metrics demonstrate standard midrange performance. This high-density bare-metal configuration suits massive containerization, CI/CD compilation farms, scalable web services, and distributed in-memory data architectures requiring hypervisor-free execution.
